title: Fingerprint launches Bot Directory for the AI era

claims.text: On September 18, 2026, Fingerprint announced the launch of Bot Directory, a public, searchable repository of AI tools, bots, and crawlers.
The directory is continuously updated and helps users understand a bot’s identity, provider, and purpose.
Fingerprint’s Bot Detection Smart Signal helps distinguish human and automated website activities.
Users can test their own AI agents for Web Bot Auth compliance and submit them for inclusion in the directory.

scenes: The presenter remains on screen as a slow push-in accompanies animated title text, “Fingerprint Bot Directory,” with a date card reading “September 18, 2026.”
The camera cuts to a graphic of a searchable directory interface as labeled icons for AI tools, bots, crawlers, and automated traffic populate the screen.
The camera moves across animated directory cards showing “Identity,” “Provider,” and “Purpose,” while a split-screen graphic contrasts “Human activity” with “Automated activity.”
The camera cuts to a simulated agent testing panel with “Web Bot Auth” and “Submit for inclusion” graphics, ending on a wide shot with the title “The AI-shaped web.”
script: If you track how automation is changing the web, you can now explore Fingerprint’s new Bot Directory. On September 18, 2026, Fingerprint announced the public resource as a searchable, continuously updated directory of AI tools, bots, crawlers, and other automated traffic. You can use it to see a bot’s identity, provider, and purpose, while Fingerprint’s Bot Detection Smart Signal helps distinguish human activity from automated activity. You can also test your own AI agents for Web Bot Auth compliance and submit them for inclusion. It is a practical window into an internet increasingly shaped by software acting on your behalf.
